questions.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific is so big that all the land on Earth could fit inside it.

questions.question: On which continent is the Sahara Desert?
questions.explanation: The Sahara is nearly as big as the whole of the United States.

questions.question: Which famous mountain is this?
questions.explanation: Mount Fuji is Japan's highest mountain, and it is actually a volcano.

questions.question: Which river flows through Egypt?
questions.explanation: Most of Egypt is desert, so almost everyone there lives close to the Nile.

questions.question: Which continent is almost completely covered in ice?
questions.explanation: About nine tenths of all the ice on Earth is in Antarctica.

questions.question: In which country is this giant rock?
questions.explanation: Uluru is sacred to the Anangu, the Aboriginal people of the area, and it seems to change colour at sunset.

media.alt: A huge red rock in a flat landscape

questions.question: Mount Everest sits on the border between Nepal and which other country?
questions.explanation: The border between Nepal and China runs right over the top of Everest.

questions.question: Which is the smallest of the world's five oceans?
questions.explanation: Much of the Arctic Ocean is covered in sea ice for most of the year.

questions.question: Which country is shaped like a boot?
questions.explanation: Italy's boot even looks as if it is about to kick a ball: the island of Sicily.

questions.question: Most of the Amazon rainforest is in which country?
questions.explanation: About 60 per cent of the Amazon rainforest is in Brazil.

questions.question: Which is the biggest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Russia is so wide that it stretches across 11 time zones.

questions.question: Which famous waterfall is this?
questions.explanation: Local people call Victoria Falls 'the smoke that thunders' because of its huge clouds of spray.

media.alt: A wide waterfall with clouds of spray
media.credit: Photo: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Turkey is partly in which two continents?
questions.explanation: The city of Istanbul is split between Europe and Asia by a narrow strip of sea called the Bosphorus.

questions.question: What is the name of the imaginary line around the middle of the Earth?
questions.explanation: The country of Ecuador is named after the equator, which runs through it.

questions.question: Mount Etna is a volcano on which island?
questions.explanation: Etna is one of the most active volcanoes in the world and erupts often.

questions.question: The River Danube flows into which sea?
questions.explanation: On its way to the Black Sea the Danube passes through four capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade.

questions.question: Lake Titicaca lies on the border between Peru and which country?
questions.explanation: At about 3,800 metres up, Titicaca is often called the highest navigable lake in the world.

questions.question: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
questions.explanation: Canada's coastline is over 200,000 kilometres long, thanks largely to its thousands of Arctic islands.

questions.question: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.explanation: Lesotho is also the only country in the world that lies entirely above 1,000 metres.

questions.question: The Atacama, one of the driest deserts on Earth, is mostly in which country?
questions.explanation: NASA has tested Mars rovers in the Atacama because its soil is so like the surface of Mars.

questions.question: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Siberia's Lake Baikal holds about a fifth of all the unfrozen fresh water on the Earth's surface.

questions.question: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Spain from which country?
questions.explanation: At its narrowest the strait is only about 14 kilometres wide, so on a clear day you can see Africa from Europe.

questions.question: Which mountain is this?
questions.explanation: The Matterhorn's famous pyramid peak sits on the border between Switzerland and Italy.

media.credit: Photo: chil, on Camptocamp.org Derivative work:Zacharie Grossen, CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: In which country is this mountain, the highest in Africa?
questions.explanation: Kilimanjaro is a dormant volcano, and its summit, Uhuru Peak, is 5,895 metres high.

media.alt: A snow-topped mountain rising above grassland
media.credit: Photo: Sergey Pesterev, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Mount Kosciuszko is the highest mountain on which continent's mainland?
questions.explanation: It was named by the Polish explorer Paul Strzelecki after the Polish-Lithuanian hero Tadeusz Kościuszko.

questions.question: The shores of which body of water are the lowest land on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Dead Sea is so salty that swimmers float on it without even trying.

questions.question: Which river carries more water than any other in the world?
questions.explanation: The Amazon pours about a fifth of all the fresh water that rivers carry into the world's oceans.

questions.question: Greenland is a self-governing part of which country?
questions.explanation: Greenland is the largest island in the world that is not a continent.

questions.question: The River Ganges flows into which body of water?
questions.explanation: Its delta, shared with the Brahmaputra, is the largest river delta in the world.

questions.question: The Mekong River reaches the sea in which country?
questions.explanation: In Vietnam the Mekong splits into so many channels that it is called the River of Nine Dragons.
